result.headline: Roll control degraded from ~t=61 s; roll actuators 4/5 froze at 1500 us from 65.9 s; cause unresolved
result.explanation: A control fault is visible: roll tracking worsens from ~61 s, with large roll-setpoint swings and a slow roll response. Outputs ch4/ch5 freeze at neutral from 65.92 s. Data cannot say whether guidance, actuator or sensing is the cause.

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] followed its setpoint worse from t=60.966 to 101.61 s: typical |error| up to 48.598 deg against 6.1 over the whole recording
evidence.shows: Roll tracking degrades from ~61 s and stays degraded to the end of the recording

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[4]] held 1500 from t=65.92 to 101.49 s (109 samples)
evidence.shows: ch4 stops moving at neutral from 65.92 s; ch5 does the same (line 26) and was identical to ch4 before the freeze

evidence.quote: CHANGE control.attitude_setpoint[roll] at t=77.737 s: 40.12 -> -39.55 deg (step -79.67, 569.1x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The roll setpoint itself makes ~80 deg swings; the vehicle lags them by several seconds

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.538 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: Sensor-health error and low-voltage warning at start only, never repeated; the only controller events in the recording

checked.check: Order in which signals left baseline around the onset
checked.result: The roll setpoint left baseline at 58.249 s, ch3/4/5 at 58.38 s, vehicle roll at 59.51 s. The ch4/5 freeze at 65.92 s comes after degradation began.
checked.about: Frozen ch4/5 as the original trigger

checked.check: Roll setpoint vs ch3 output in the late stretch
checked.result: Correlation 0.897 at lag -0.329 s: ch3 follows the roll command, so the command path to ch3 works

checked.check: Roll setpoint vs ch1 output in the late stretch
checked.result: Correlation 0.053: ch1 is not a roll channel

checked.check: ch3 output vs vehicle roll, before and after the onset
checked.result: Correlation -0.275 before the onset and -0.202 after it; the relation did not change
checked.about: A new actuator or surface failure on ch3

checked.result: ch4 and ch5 are identical at every sample; both go to 1500 from 66.347 s while the roll setpoint keeps moving (14.62 then 21.39 deg)
checked.about: Output or actuator fault on ch4/5

checked.check: Roll response in the 76-82 s window
checked.result: Setpoint went from 44.87 at 76.076 s to -44.97 at 79.596 s; vehicle roll peaked at 45.236 at 77.628 s and fell to -0.027 at 81.989 s. The response lags the command by about 3 s.
checked.about: Guidance swings plus slow roll response

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[yaw] at t=61.696 s: -16.442 -> -87.801 deg (step -71.359, 97.5x its usual variation)
effects.why: Yaw and velocity steps follow the roll excursions (lines 61, 70, 68), so they are consequences of the manoeuvre

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.velocity[y] at t=62.207 s: 14.645 -> -2.155 m/s (step -16.8, 80x its usual variation)
effects.why: Follows the roll and yaw excursion; it starts after roll left baseline

effects.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[yaw] typical |error| by stretch: 0-10.161 s 53.077, 10.161-20.322 s 74.645
effects.why: Yaw error is large for the whole recording, including before the onset; the setpoint is unwrapped (452-468 deg) so it cannot be read as a fault

next_action.action: Bench-test ch4/ch5 outputs and servos with props off; confirm channel mapping
next_action.why: Separates a dead or frozen roll output or servo from a guidance or sensing cause, and shows what ch4/5 are mapped to.
how: Read the output mapping: which surfaces ch1, ch3, ch4, ch5 drive
Power the vehicle with props removed, command a roll setpoint of +-40 deg and watch the servos on ch4/ch5
Compare servo travel to ch3 and log actuator.output[ch[4]], [ch[5]], [ch[3]]
Check the servo power rail voltage under load and the ch4/5 connectors
next_action.conditions: On the ground, battery at normal charge, props removed, motor disarmed; a qualified engineer reviews before powering servos.
next_action.baseline: ch3 response to the same command, and the ch4/ch5 sweep in this recording (cc_14)

outcomes.label: ch4/5 servos do not move
outcomes.means: Output or servo or wiring fault on the roll surfaces; the freeze is a failure rather than a consequence.
outcomes.then: Inspect servo, connector and power rail

outcomes.label: ch4/5 move normally on the bench
outcomes.means: Output hardware is fine; the freeze came from software or a mode change, so look at the controller.
outcomes.then: Request flight-mode log and controller parameters

unknowns: Which surfaces ch1, ch3, ch4 and ch5 drive; the data shows no mapping
Why the roll setpoint swings +-45 deg in single samples late in the flight
Whether the 1500 us freeze is a controller output hold, a failsafe or a recording artefact

already_answered.answer: Roll tracking degraded from about 61 s and stayed degraded to the end of the recording.

data_requests.what: Flight-mode and failsafe log, controller parameters and mixer output mapping for the flight
data_requests.window: Whole flight, especially around the freeze
data_requests.why_needed: Shows whether a mode change or failsafe froze ch4/5, and what ch1/ch3/ch4/ch5 drive

unobservable.fact: Physical state of roll servos, linkages and servo power rail
unobservable.why_it_matters: Decides whether the ch4/5 freeze is a hardware fault or a controller hold
unobservable.how_to_observe: Bench-command servos and measure rail voltage under load

hypotheses.claim: Outputs ch4/ch5 stopped working at 65.92 s, leaving roll control to ch3 alone.
hypotheses.because: The freeze is exact and both channels were identical, but it starts after roll degradation began.

hypotheses.claim: Large, fast roll setpoints (+-45 deg in a single sample) outpace the airframe response and create the tracking error.
hypotheses.because: Setpoint steps of 80 deg (line 49) match the worst tracking errors, and ch3 follows them with correlation 0.897.
hypotheses.observed_at: controller setpoint and actuator output records

hypotheses.claim: Faulty attitude or airspeed sensing corrupts the estimate the controller uses.
hypotheses.because: A sensor-health error was logged at start, and airspeed and yaw rate are constant 0 for the whole recording (lines 29, 30).
The low-voltage warning appears once at 0.538 s and not again; roll tracking was good before the onset.

events.what: Low-voltage warning and sensor-health error at start
events.why: Only controller events; never repeated, so their link to the later fault is unknown

events.what: Roll setpoint swings of 58-88 deg in one step
events.why: Largest roll tracking errors coincide with these swings

events.what: ch4 and ch5 frozen at 1500 us from 65.92 s
events.why: Roll outputs stop responding while the setpoint keeps moving

events.what: Yaw and velocity steps after 61 s

events.why: Unused channels held constant for the whole recording

result.lesson: No earlier cases apply; none exist in the workspace.
